questions.questionText: Which statement about a production possibility curve is correct?

options.text: A production possibility curve is an alternative name for an industry supply curve.
A production possibility curve is an economic model of potential output.
A realistic production possibility curve must be drawn as a straight line.
A production possibility curve applies only to an economy’s production of goods.

questions.questionText: Which firm is likely to find it most difficult to expand the use of its main factor of production?

options.text: a farm growing crops in extensive fields
a technology firm dependent on risky innovations
a textile firm making use of labour-intensive systems
an engineering firm relying upon capital-intensive methods

questions.questionText:
A government taxes the production of cars.
What is likely to decrease?

options.text: the cost of supplying cars
the price of cars
the revenue for the government
the supply of cars at every price

questions.questionText: Which pair of economic institutions can be found in a market economy?

options.text: local government and charities
monopolies and commercial banks
nationalised industries and partnerships
stock exchange and public corporations

questions.questionText:
Developers want to increase the size of a major retail shopping area in a city. It is thought that the
proposal would create hundreds of jobs, be profitable for the shops but cause major traffic
congestion.
What economic concepts are directly involved in this statement?

options.text: external cost and private benefit
income distribution and inelastic demand
private investment and a decrease in supply
social benefit and perfect competition

questions.questionText: What does the term ‘closed shop’ mean?

options.text: a bankrupt retail establishment
a trade union that is approved by the government
an agreement that all workers must be members of the same trade union
an agreement by trade unions to share members

economies of scale

questions.questionText: What function does a central bank fulfil?

options.text: It issues currency.
It offers overdraft facilities to individuals.
It operates deposit accounts.
It raises taxation.

questions.questionText:
The table shows how three people spend their income.
person X person Y person Z
food, clothing and housing 30% 25% 50%
entertainment and leisure 35% 35% 25%
luxury goods 35% 40% 25%
For these three people, what is the most likely order of income, from lowest income to highest
income?

options.text: Y → X → Z
Y → Z → X
Z → X → Y
Z → Y → X

questions.questionText: How does a firm guarantee that it makes the maximum profit?

options.text: by maximising the difference between its total revenue and total cost
by maximising the number of goods that it sells
by minimising the number of goods that it keeps in stock
by minimising the difference between average revenue and average cost

questions.questionText: What is true when comparing a monopoly to a perfectly competitive firm?

options.text: Monopolies will have perfect knowledge of their market.
Monopoly costs are always lower owing to economies of scale.
Monopoly price is likely to be higher.
The products that monopolies produce have more limited demand.

questions.questionText:
A government wishes to stimulate economic recovery.
Which action will assist this?

options.text: decreasing government investment
decreasing income tax
increasing indirect taxation
increasing interest rates

questions.questionText:
When a government aims to encourage economic growth it may adopt supply-side policies.
Which policy is a supply-side policy?

options.text: increasing the money supply
lowering interest rates
reducing direct taxation
retraining unemployed workers

questions.questionText:
Which policy combination will be the most effective if a government wishes to increase the level
of employment?

options.text: decrease general taxation and increase the rate of interest
decrease general taxation and decrease the rate of interest
increase general taxation and decrease the rate of interest
increase general taxation and increase the rate of interest.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to lead to a rise in the rate of inflation?

options.text: a decrease in consumer spending
a decrease in unemployment benefits
an increase in import prices
an increase in income tax

questions.questionText:
Which measures, in addition to Gross Domestic Product per capita, are included in the Human
Development Index?

options.text: average earnings and inequalities of incomes
balance of trade and balance of payments
life expectancy at birth and expected years of schooling
size of population and age structure of population

questions.questionText:
The table gives information about three economic indicators in four countries.
inflation interest rates unemployment
% % %
country W 1.4 3.4 10.2
country X 3.7 8.7 12.3
country Y 3.6 7.3 14.2
country Z 2.1 6.0 7.7
What may be concluded from this information?

options.text: Countries with higher inflation have higher interest rates.
Countries with higher interest rates have lower unemployment.
The country with the lowest inflation had the highest unemployment.
The country with the lowest unemployment had the lowest inflation.

questions.questionText: Which type of government policy would be most suitable to control external costs of production?

options.text: employment policy
fiscal policy
monetary policy
trade policy

questions.questionText: Why might the emigration of workers help the economy of a developing country?

options.text: The dependency ratio is likely to improve.
The inflow of transfers of money is likely to increase.
The least healthy workers are likely to be the last ones to leave.
The more skilled workers are likely to be the ones to leave.

questions.questionText:
What combination of changes in the birth rate and death rate is most likely to increase the
dependency ratio in a country?
birth rate death rate

options.text: falls falls
falls rises
rises falls
rises rises

questions.questionText: What might cause the balance on the current account of Mauritius to improve?

options.text: increased purchases of coffee from Kenya
increased transport of Mauritian goods in Greek ships
increased spending by Mauritians on holidays in South Africa
increased spending by tourists in Mauritian hotels

questions.questionText:
A country says that it wishes to increase its trade protection policies.
What might that involve?

options.text: conservation of resources and taxes on external costs
eliminating waste in the use of resources and grants to multinational companies
increased self sufficiency and increased tariffs
price controls and increased regulations on domestic monopoly industries

questions.questionText:
It has been suggested that all countries producing arms should ban the export of weapons and
cut production in order to reduce the risk of war.
What would happen if this occurred?

options.text: The balance of payments on current account of countries exporting weapons would immediately improve.
The price of existing weapons would fall.
There would be a risk of structural unemployment in countries that are major producers of weapons.
There would be no overall effect on the balance of payments as countries would produce their own weapons.
